title: C# Questions & Answers - Byte Stream
sourceFile: Byte Stream - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses in detail on byte stream in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of these classes is used to read and write bytes in a file?
Which of these data types is returned by every method of OutputStream?
questions.explanation: Every method of OutputStream returns void and throws an IOExeption in case of errors.

questions.question: Which of these classes is used for input and output operation when working with bytes?
questions.explanation: InputStream & OutputStream are designed for byte stream. Reader and writer are designed for character stream.

questions.question: Which among the following is used for storage of memory aspects?
questions.explanation: A byte stream that uses memory for storage.

questions.question: Which among the following is used for storage of unmanaged memory aspects?
questions.explanation:
A byte stream that uses unmanaged memory for storage.

questions.question: Which property among the following represents the current position of the stream?
questions.explanation: This property contains the length of the stream. This property is read-only.

questions.question: Choose the filemode method which is used to create a new output file with the condition that the file with same name must not exist.
questions.explanation: Creates a new output file. The file must not already be existing.

questions.question: Choose the filemode method which is used to create a new output file with the condition that the file with same name if exists will destroy the old file:
questions.explanation: Creates a new output file. Any pre-existing file with the same name will be destroyed.

questions.question: Which of these is a method used to clear all the data present in output buffers?
Which of these is a method used for reading bytes from the file?
questions.explanation: FileStream defines two methods that reads bytes from a file: ReadByte() and Read().
